language: Python 3.11+ standard library (CI runs 3.14) and Bash build scripts
summary: toolchains builds the compilers and runtimes that qq builds use, currently CPython and Node.js with pnpm, publishes them to a registry, and pins each by content digest. A build then refers to a toolchain only by that digest, and a new one reaches products only after a reviewed promotion.

how_it_works.title: A spec per toolchain
how_it_works.text: Each toolchain is a toolchain.toml with its version, upstream source URLs and sha256 checksums, smoke-test commands and pinned consumer repos, plus a build.sh. qqtc builds it into a reproducible tarball with a fixed timestamp.

how_it_works.title: Build, smoke-test, stage
how_it_works.text: The build workflow builds and smoke-tests every toolchain on pull requests. On main it also pushes each one to ghcr.io/quirq-ai/toolchains/<name> with a staging tag as a single-layer OCI artifact, signs build provenance, then builds the pinned consumer repos with it.

how_it_works.title: Promotion by reviewed PR
how_it_works.text: qqtc promote writes the staged digest into promoted.toml in one canonical form. The promotion-gate check verifies the provenance came from build.yml on main, that the manifest is exactly one toolchain layer, and re-runs smoke tests and consumer builds on the pulled bytes.

how_it_works.title: The gate judges with main's tools
how_it_works.text: On a pull request, promotion-gate runs main's copy of gate.py, qqtc and the specs, reading the PR's files only as data. It also refuses workflows that could fake the check, such as one that can write checks or statuses.

Only one platform is supported: qqtc accepts linux-x86_64 and nothing else.
The CPython build links the runner's shared libraries such as OpenSSL and libffi, so it is not yet hermetic.
promotion-gate is advisory today. gate's settings at its current main already list it as a required check on toolchains; it becomes required when those settings are next applied.
